meaning: Airflow was not proven while the unit was in the ignition cycle.
causes: Blower stopped on thermal or current overload
Blocked blower inlet or inlet air filter
Blockage in or defective Blower Proof switch or Blocked Inlet switch
Loose temperature (AUX) connection in I/O box or defective temperature sensor
Loose 0-10 V wire from I/O box to blower, defective I/O box, wrong 0-10 V output selection, defective air-fuel valve potentiometer
Hard light
checks: Check the blower for excess heat or high current that may trip an overload.
Inspect the blower inlet and air filter at the air/fuel valve.
Remove and inspect the Blower Proof and Blocked Inlet switches; clean or replace. Check continuity with the blower running; replace if erratic or above zero ohms.
Check inlet air temperature and the AUX input voltage in the I/O box against the Appendix C table.
Measure the I/O box 0-10 V output (10 V equals 100 percent open valve) and check the Analog Out option is Valve Position 0-10V.
Check air/fuel valve position at 0, 50 and 100 percent against the dial; check igniter-injector for soot or electrode erosion.

meaning: Airflow was not proven during the purge.
causes: Blower not running or too slow
Defective or blocked Blocked Inlet switch or air filter
Blocked blower inlet or ductwork
No voltage to the Blocked Inlet switch from the C-More controller
Causes 3 to 12 of AIRFLOW FAULT DURING IGNITION also apply
checks: Start the unit; if the blower does not run, check the blower solid-state relay input and output voltage, then the blower.
If it runs, turn the unit off and check the Blocked Inlet switch for continuity; replace if none.
Remove and inspect the air filter and switch for blockage; inspect the blower inlet and ductwork.
During start, verify 24 VAC from each side of the switch to ground; if absent refer to qualified service personnel.

meaning: Airflow was lost while the unit was running.
causes: Blower stopped on thermal or current overload
Blocked blower inlet, ductwork, air filter or Blocked Inlet switch
Defective Blocked Inlet switch
Combustion oscillations
Causes 3 to 16 of AIRFLOW FAULT DURING IGNITION also apply
checks: Check the blower for excess heat or high current draw.
Inspect the inlet and ductwork; clean or replace the air filter and switch.
Verify 24 VAC from each side of the switch to ground; if not present at both sides replace the switch.
Run to full fire; if the unit rumbles or runs rough, perform combustion calibration.

meaning: The delayed interlock circuit is open.
causes: Delayed interlock jumper not properly installed or missing
Device proving switch hooked to the interlock is not closed
checks: Check that the jumper is installed across the delayed interlock terminals in the I/O box.

If two external wires are on the terminals, check that an end switch for a proving device (pump, louver, etc.) is functional. A jumper may be temporarily installed to test the interlock; remove it afterwards.

meaning: The direct drive signal is not present or is wrong.
causes: Signal not installed, wrong polarity, defective at source or loose wiring
Signal not isolated (floating)
C-More signal type switches not set for voltage or current
checks: Check the I/O box connection, polarity and signal level, and wiring continuity from the source.
Check the signal is isolated at the source.
Check the DIP switch on the PMC board and the control signal type in the Configuration menu.

meaning: Flame was lost or not detected during the ignition trial.
causes: Worn flame detector
No spark from the spark igniter or defective ignition transformer
Defective IGST board or SSOV
Pilot scanner failed, pilot view port blocked, pilot gas valve closed, pilot solenoid not opening, clogged pilot ignition piece
Carbon or debris on the burner
checks: Before starting, refer to the Figure 5-4 flow chart at the end of the chapter.
Remove and inspect the flame detector; replace if worn.
Close the internal gas valve and arc a spark igniter outside the unit; if no spark check for 120 VAC at the transformer primary during ignition.
Check the SSOV opens (120 VAC at its terminals); if not and no voltage, suspect the IGST board.

Check the scanner red LED goes from flashing to steady with a small flame; clean the pilot view port; open the pilot gas valve; listen for the pilot solenoid; inspect the ignition piece; inspect the burner with a borescope and clean.

meaning: Flame was lost while the unit was running.
causes: Worn flame detector or cracked ceramic
Defective regulator
Poor combustion calibration
Debris on burner or blocked condensate drain
Main flame detector touching the burner mesh
checks: Inspect the flame detector for wear or cracked ceramic; replace if necessary.
Check gas pressure into and out of the air/fuel valve.
Check combustion calibration per Section 4.5 of the installation and startup guide.
Inspect the burner for carbon or debris and clean; clear the condensate drain.
Straighten or replace the main flame detector.

meaning: The heat demand relays on the ignition/stepper board did not respond correctly.
causes: Heat demand relays on the IGST board failed to activate when commanded
Relay activated when not in demand
checks: Press CLEAR and restart; if the fault persists replace the IGST board.
A defective relay means replacing the IGST board.

meaning: Exhaust temperature is high.
causes: Poor combustion calibration
Carboned heat exchanger due to incorrect combustion calibration
checks: Check combustion calibration per Section 4.5 of the installation and startup guide.
If exhaust temperature is above 200 F (93.3 C) check calibration; calibrate or repair as necessary.

meaning: Gas pressure fault due to high gas pressure.
causes: Incorrect supply gas pressure
Defective SSOV actuator
Defective high gas pressure switch
checks: Ensure gas pressure at the SSOV inlet does not exceed 14 in. W.C. (3487 Pa).
If downstream pressure cannot be lowered with the adjustment screw to the range in the installation and startup guide, the SSOV actuator may be defective.
Remove the switch leads and check continuity across C and NC with the unit not firing; replace the switch if none.

meaning: The high water temperature switch has opened.
causes: Faulty water temperature switch
Incorrect PID settings or faulty shell temperature sensor
Unit in MANUAL mode, or setpoint above the over-temperature switch setpoint
System flow changes faster than the unit can respond
Refractory failure
VFD in Local mode or voltage dropped below threshold
checks: Test that the switch trips at its actual setting.
Compare PID settings with menu defaults; if changed, record them and reset to defaults.
Measure shell and BTU sensor resistance at a known water temperature using the Appendix C charts.
If in MANUAL, switch to AUTO; confirm the switch is set above the unit setpoint.
On variable flow systems monitor flow changes.
Refractory switches on the end plates are in series with the limit; replace the refractory at the hottest end plate. Check incoming voltage and set the VFD to Remote.

meaning: The unit has exceeded its high water temperature limit.
causes: Causes listed under HIGH WATER TEMP SWITCH OPEN
Temp HI Limit setting too low
checks: See HIGH WATER TEMP SWITCH OPEN.
Check the Temp HI Limit setting.

meaning: Communication fault between the PMC board and the ignition/stepper (IGST) board.
causes: Communication fault between the PMC board and the IGST board
checks: Press CLEAR and restart; if the fault persists contact qualified service personnel.

meaning: The ignition position switch is closed when the air/fuel valve should be in the purge position.
causes: Air/fuel valve not rotating
Defective or shorted switch, or switch wired incorrectly
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: Start the unit; the air/fuel valve should rotate to purge (open). If not, check its calibration; if calibration is fine the problem may be the valve or controller, refer to qualified service personnel.
If it rotates to purge, check the ignition switch for continuity between N.O. and COM when not on the cam; replace if it shows continuity.
Check wiring (wire numbers on the N.O. terminals).
Check DS1 and DS2 LEDs on the power supply board (steady on) and the IGST heartbeat LED DS1 (blinking each second); replace the board if not.

meaning: The ignition position switch is open when the air/fuel valve should be in the ignition position.
causes: Air/fuel valve not rotating to ignition position
Defective ignition switch
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: Start the unit; the valve should go to purge then back toward closed. If not, check calibration, then refer to qualified service personnel.
Check the ignition position switch for continuity between N.O. and COM when on the cam.
Check DS1 and DS2 LEDs on the power supply board and the IGST heartbeat LED.

meaning: The interlock circuit is open.
causes: Interlock jumper not installed or removed
Energy Management System does not have the unit enabled
Device proving switch on the interlock is not closed
checks: Check a jumper is installed across the interlock terminals in the I/O box.

If there are two external wires, check whether an Energy Management system has the unit disabled. A jumper may be temporarily installed to see whether the interlock circuit works; remove it afterwards.
Check that the proving switch for any device on the interlock closes and that the device is operational.

meaning: Line voltage is wired out of phase.
causes: Line and neutral switched in the AC power box
Incorrect power supply transformer wiring
checks: Check hot and neutral in the AC power box are not reversed.
Check transformer wiring against the power box wiring diagram.

meaning: Gas pressure fault due to low gas pressure.
causes: Incorrect supply gas pressure
Defective low gas pressure switch
checks: Measure natural gas pressure upstream of the SSOV actuator(s) with the unit firing; the minimum is 14 in. W.C. (3.5 kPa), though the BMK 6000 can operate derated at 11 in. W.C. and the BMK 5000 at 10 in. W.C.
Measure at the low gas pressure switch; if it is above 10 in. W.C. check continuity across the switch and replace if necessary.

meaning: The water level circuit reports low water.
causes: Insufficient water level in the system
Defective water level circuitry
Defective water level probe
checks: Check the system for sufficient water.
Test the circuitry with the C-More LOW WATER TEST and RESET buttons; replace the circuitry if it does not respond.
Check continuity from the probe end to the shell; change the probe if none.

meaning: The unit is not receiving information from the Modbus network.
causes: Unit not seeing information from the Modbus network
checks: Check network connections; if the fault persists contact qualified service personnel.

meaning: The oxygen reading is low.
causes: Dirty air filter or blocked inlet air duct
Gas pressure too high
Blocked flue or blocked condensate trap
Blower failure or VFD failure
checks: Clean the air filter per Section 4.10 and inspect the duct.
Measure gas pressure between the SSOV and air/fuel valve; it should be 7.9 in. W.C. plus or minus 0.2.
Check the flue and the condensate trap (Section 4.9).
Check blower speed with a strobe against VFD Hz (RPM = 57.5 x Hz); check the VFD using the VFD manufacturer documentation.

meaning: The oxygen sensor reads below -4 percent or above 24 percent.
causes: O2 reading less than -4 percent or greater than 24 percent
checks: Check the O2 offset and gain values in the Calibration menu; if they are 1.0 and 1024 respectively, replace the O2 sensor.

meaning: The oxygen reading is out of range.
causes: Combustion calibration incorrect
Blocked inlet air duct or louver
checks: Check with a combustion analyzer and recalibrate.
Unblock the air inlet and measure the open area for combustion air to the room.

meaning: Fault with the outdoor temperature sensor.
causes: Loose or broken wiring
Defective or incorrect sensor
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring.
Check sensor resistance against specification.
Confirm the correct sensor is installed.

meaning: The purge position switch is closed during ignition.
causes: Air/fuel valve rotated to purge and did not return to the ignition position
Defective or shorted switch, or switch wired incorrectly
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: Start the unit; the valve should go to purge then back toward closed. If not, check calibration and refer to qualified service personnel.
If it returns, check the purge switch for continuity between N.O. and COM when not on the cam and check its wiring; replace if wired correctly.
Check power supply board DS1 and DS2 LEDs and the IGST heartbeat LED.

meaning: The purge position switch did not close during purge.
causes: Defective purge switch
No voltage at switch, or switch wired incorrectly
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: If the air/fuel valve rotates, check the purge switch for continuity when closing; replace if none.
Measure 24 VAC from each side of the switch to ground; if absent refer to qualified service personnel.
Check wiring and the power supply and IGST board LEDs.

meaning: The internal recirculation pump has failed.
causes: Internal recirculation pump failed
checks: Replace the recirculation pump.

meaning: The remote setpoint signal is not present or is wrong.
causes: Signal not installed, wrong polarity, defective at source or loose wiring
Signal not isolated (floating) if 4 to 20 mA
C-More signal type switches not set for voltage or current
checks: Check the I/O box connection, polarity, signal level and wiring continuity.
Check isolation at the source.
Check the PMC DIP switch and the control signal type in the Configuration menu.

meaning: Flame is detected when none should be present.
causes: Defective flame detector
SSOV not fully closed
checks: Replace the flame detector.
Check the SSOV open/close indicator window and confirm it is fully closed; if not, replace the valve or actuator.

Close the 2 in. gas shut-off valve downstream of the SSOV, install a manometer at the leak detection port between the SSOV and shut-off valve; if there is a pressure reading replace the SSOV valve or actuator.

meaning: The safety shut-off valve fault occurred during purge.
causes: See SSOV SWITCH OPEN
checks: See SSOV SWITCH OPEN.

meaning: The SSOV switch closed for 15 seconds during the run.
causes: SSOV switch closed for 15 seconds during run
checks: Replace the actuator.

meaning: The SSOV relay on the IGST board has failed or the SSOV is miswired.
causes: SSOV relay failed on the IGST board
Floating neutral
Hot and neutral reversed at the SSOV
checks: Press CLEAR and restart; if the fault persists replace the IGST board.
Neutral and earth ground must be connected at the source; the measured voltage between them should be near zero, no more than a few millivolts.
Check the SSOV power wiring.

meaning: The SSOV proof-of-closure switch does not show the valve closed.
causes: Actuator not allowing full closure of the gas valve
SSOV powered when it should not be
Defective switch or actuator, or incorrectly wired switch
checks: Observe the SSOV indicator and confirm the valve fully closes.
If the SSOV never closes it may be powered continuously: close the gas supply, remove power and refer to qualified service personnel.
Remove the SSOV electrical cover and check switch continuity with the gas valve closed; adjust or replace the switch or actuator.
Confirm the proof-of-closure switch is correctly wired.

meaning: The air/fuel valve stepper motor is not responding correctly.
causes: Air/fuel valve out of calibration or unplugged
Loose wiring to the stepper motor or defective motor
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: Perform the Stepper Feedback Calibration procedure (C-More User Manual OMM-0032, Section 6.2.1).
Check the air/fuel valve is connected and inspect connections at the motor and harness.
Replace the stepper motor if defective.
Check power supply board DS1 and DS2 LEDs and the IGST heartbeat LED.

meaning: The SSOV did not open during ignition.
causes: SSOV did not open
checks: Check the pilot assembly for carbon buildup.
Check the scanners sensed the pilot flame.
Check power through the ignition relay.
Scanners close the neutral side of the relay coil.

meaning: Airflow was not proven while the unit was in the ignition cycle.
causes: Blower stopped on thermal or current overload
Blocked blower inlet or ductwork, blocked or defective Blower Proof switch or blocked-air inlet switch
Loose temperature (AUX) connection or defective temperature sensor
Loose 0-10 V wire to the blower, defective I/O box, wrong 0-10 V output selection or defective air-fuel valve potentiometer
checks: Check the blower for excess heat or high current.
Inspect the inlet and ductwork; remove and inspect, clean or replace the proof and blocked-air inlet switches. Check continuity with the blower running; replace if erratic or above zero ohms.
Check inlet air temperature and AUX input voltage against Appendix C.
Measure the I/O box 0-10 V output (8.2 V equals 100 percent open valve) and check Analog Out is Valve Position 0-10V.
Check air/fuel valve position at 0, 50 and 100 percent against the dial.

meaning: Airflow was not proven during purge.
causes: Blower not running or too slow
Defective or blocked air flow switch, or blocked blower inlet or ductwork
No voltage to the switch from the control box
Causes 3 to 12 of AIRFLOW FAULT DURING IGNITION also apply
checks: Start the unit; if the blower does not run check the blower solid-state relay, then the blower.
If it runs, check the airflow switch for continuity; replace if none.
Remove and inspect the switch for blockage; inspect the blower inlet and ductwork.
Measure 24 VAC from each side of the switch to ground during start; if absent refer to qualified service personnel.

meaning: Airflow was lost while running.
causes: Blower stopped on thermal or current overload
Blocked blower inlet, ductwork or airflow switch
Defective airflow switch
Combustion oscillations
checks: Check the blower for excess heat or high current.
Inspect the inlet and ductwork; inspect and clean or replace the airflow switch.
Check airflow switch continuity with the blower running; replace if erratic or above zero ohms.
Run to full fire; if the unit rumbles or runs rough, perform combustion calibration.

meaning: The delayed interlock circuit is open.
causes: Delayed interlock jumper not installed or removed
Device proving switch on the interlock is not closed
checks: Check a jumper is installed across the delayed interlock terminals in the I/O box.
If two external wires are on the terminals, check the end switch for a device such as a pump or louver. A jumper may be temporarily installed to test the interlock; remove it afterwards.

meaning: Flame was lost or not detected during the ignition trial.
causes: Burner ground screw not installed or loose
Worn flame detector
No spark from the spark plug, or defective ignition transformer
Defective IGST board or defective SSOV
Carbon or debris on the burner
Staged ignition ball valve closed, solenoid valve not opening, or clogged staged ignition piece
checks: Inspect and retighten the burner ground screw.
Remove and inspect the flame detector for wear.
Close the internal gas valve and arc a spark igniter outside the unit; if no spark check for 120 VAC at the transformer primary during ignition.
Observe the SSOV indicator opening while arcing; if it does not open check 120 VAC at its terminals; if absent the IGST board may be defective.
Remove the burner and inspect for carbon or debris.
Open the ball valve downstream of the SSOV; listen for the solenoid valve clicking; inspect the staged ignition piece for blockage.

meaning: Flame was lost while running.
causes: Worn flame detector or cracked ceramic
Defective regulator
Poor combustion calibration
Debris on burner
Blocked condensate drain
checks: Inspect the flame detector for wear or cracked ceramic; replace if necessary.
Check gas pressure into and out of the air/fuel valve.
Check combustion calibration.
Remove the burner and inspect for carbon or debris.
Remove any blockage in the condensate drain.

meaning: The heat demand relays on the ignition/stepper board did not respond correctly.
causes: Heat demand relays on the IGST board failed to activate
Relay activated when not in demand
checks: Press CLEAR and restart; if it persists replace the IGST board.
A defective relay means replacing the IGST board.

meaning: Exhaust temperature is high.
causes: Poor combustion calibration
Heat exchanger has scale
checks: Check combustion calibration using the procedures in Chapter 4.
Clean the heat exchanger using the procedures in Chapter 6.

meaning: Gas pressure is high.
causes: Incorrect supply gas pressure
Defective SSOV actuator
Defective high gas pressure switch
checks: Ensure gas pressure at the SSOV inlet is 2 psig maximum.
If pressure downstream of the SSOV actuator cannot be lowered below 3.0 in. W.C. with the adjustment screw, the actuator may be defective.
Remove the switch leads and check continuity across common and normally closed with the unit not firing; replace if none.

meaning: The high water temperature switch has opened.
causes: Faulty water temperature switch
Incorrect PID settings or faulty shell temperature sensor
Unit in Manual mode, or setpoint above the over-temperature switch setpoint
System flow changes faster than the unit can respond
checks: Test that the switch trips at its actual setting.
Compare PID settings with the menu defaults and reset if changed.
Measure shell and BTU sensor resistance at a known water temperature with the Appendix C charts.
If in Manual mode switch to Auto; confirm the switch is set above the unit setpoint.
On variable flow systems check flow rate changes.

meaning: The unit exceeded its high water temperature limit.
causes: Causes under HIGH WATER TEMP SWITCH OPEN
Temp HI Limit setting too low
checks: See HIGH WATER TEMP SWITCH OPEN.
Check the Temp HI Limit setting.

meaning: Communication fault between the PMC board and the IGST board.
causes: Communication fault between the PMC and IGST boards
checks: Press CLEAR and restart; if the fault persists contact qualified service personnel.

meaning: The ignition position switch is closed during purge.
causes: Air/fuel valve not rotating
Defective or shorted switch, switch wired incorrectly
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: Start the unit; the air/fuel valve should rotate to purge (open). If not, check its calibration, then the valve or control box.
Check the ignition switch for continuity between N.O. and COM when not on the cam; replace if it shows continuity.
Check wiring, then the power supply board LEDs DS1 and DS2 and the IGST heartbeat LED DS1.

meaning: The ignition position switch is open during ignition.
causes: Air/fuel valve not rotating to ignition position
Defective ignition switch
Defective power supply board or fuse, or defective IGST board
checks: Start the unit; the valve should go to purge then back toward closed. If not, check calibration and refer to qualified service personnel.
Check ignition switch continuity between N.O. and COM when on the cam.
Check the power supply board LEDs and the IGST heartbeat LED.

meaning: The interlock circuit is open.
causes: Interlock jumper not installed or removed
Energy Management System does not have the unit enabled
Device proving switch on the interlock is not closed
checks: Check a jumper is installed across the interlock terminals in the I/O box.
If two external wires are on the terminals, check whether an Energy Management system has the unit disabled. A jumper may be temporarily installed to test the circuit; remove it afterwards.
Check the proving switch for any device on the interlock closes and the device is operational.

meaning: Line voltage is wired out of phase.
causes: Line and neutral switched in the AC power box
Incorrect power supply transformer wiring
checks: Check hot and neutral in the AC power box are not reversed.
Check transformer wiring against the power box wiring diagram.

meaning: Gas pressure is low.
causes: Incorrect supply gas pressure
Defective low pressure gas switch
checks: Measure gas pressure upstream of the SSOV actuator(s) with the unit firing; for FM and DBB gas trains it should be between 4.0 and 14 in. W.C.
Measure at the low gas pressure switch; if above 2.6 in. W.C. check continuity across the switch and replace if necessary.
